short: A decisive naval victory by an allied Greek fleet over the invading Persian navy, halting Xerxes' advance.
full:
In September 480 BCE, following the Persian victory at Thermopylae and the sacking of Athens, the allied Greek fleet under the tactical command of Themistocles lured the massive Persian armada into the narrow straits of Salamis. The cramped conditions neutralised the Persian numerical advantage and prevented their ships from manoeuvring. The heavier Greek triremes rammed and boarded the disorganized enemy vessels, destroying much of the Persian fleet.

The defeat forced King Xerxes to retreat to Asia with the bulk of his army, fearing he might be trapped in Europe if the Greeks destroyed the pontoon bridges across the Hellespont. He left a substantial force under General Mardonius to complete the conquest of Greece, setting the stage for the final land confrontation at Plataea the following year.
